title.narrative: Strengthening capacities of ministries of education staff to effectively use and report on education data to better inform policy making and planning

description.narrative: Summary Description Monitoring progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the Caribbean region is not just important; it's absolutely essential. This monitoring serves as the compass guiding the region's journey towards sustainable development, offering insights into both the strides made and the hurdles faced along the way. However, effective and accurate monitoring of the SDGs demands a concerted effort at the local level. There's a mounting call for more comprehensive statistics delivered in a timely manner and with greater accessibility, particularly microdata. This demand reflects a growing recognition of the critical role data plays in informed decision-making and policy formulation. Yet, the path to robust monitoring is not without its challenges. Chief among these challenges is the availability and quality of data. While many Caribbean countries have made commendable progress in data collection and reporting, persistent gaps and inconsistencies persist. These shortcomings are exacerbated by the small size of Caribbean nations, which limits the level of disaggregation needed for certain indicators. Addressing the challenges of SDG monitoring in the Caribbean requires a multifaceted approach that combines technical expertise, institutional support, and cross-sectoral collaboration. This workplan aims to strengthening capacities of ministries of education staff to effectively the relevance, use and report on education data to better inform policy making and planning.
